subject: Renewal: scaleout commitment 16→32 GPUs — throughput & rate safeguards
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@bluecrest.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@bluecrest.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal coming up — interest in doubling reserved GPUs

Hi Markus,

Our contract with Redwood is up for renewal on July 15 and the infra team is asking whether we can move from the current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU committed pool for the next term. Two main asks from BlueCrest:

- Predictable throughput target: we need a firm throughput commitment for steady-state batch jobs (roughly a 2x uplift from current peak tokens/hour).
- Clear per-hour reserved pricing for the added capacity and an optional staged ramp (first 30 days at partial commit while we finish migration).

Can you share a draft amendment and indicative pricing so I can take it to procurement? We may need a 12 or 18 month term — procurement prefers 12 but wants options on automatic step-up if needed.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of ML Platforms, BlueCrest AI

[Attachment: bluecrest_capacity_profile.csv (csv)]

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-01T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — interest in doubling reserved GPUs

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads-up.

High-level we can support a move to a 32-GPU reserved pool during renewal. Initial bullets below; I'll attach an amendment draft and throughput modeling for your procurement and infra team to review.

- Reserved rate: base per-hour reserved rate for the incremental 16 GPUs at €2.95/hr/GPU (all-in for our dedicated hardware plan) — this represents a ~12% discount vs on-demand.
- Throughput guarantee: we can commit to a steady-state throughput uplift target of ~2.1x current peak (we model ~130M tokens/hour net for the full 32 pool under your existing model mix). We will define measurement windows and a monthly verification process in the SLA appendix.
- Staged ramp: first 30 days we can allow a 50% billing credit on the additional GPUs if BlueCrest chooses to do a migration/validation window (documented in amendment).
- Term options: 12- or 18-month commitments supported. Longer terms give an additional 3% discount on the incremental pool.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll drop an amendment (v3) with explicit and measurable throughput SLAs, a rate table, and a migration credit clause.
2) Aditya — can you verify the throughput modeling and token assumptions and attach a comparison for Elena’s infra team?
3) Laura — I’ll need you to own commercial redlines and the final signature path.

If the commercial team is comfortable I can schedule a 30-minute call with procurement on Friday to walk through the numbers.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
mobile: +44 7700 900111

[Attachments: redwood_amendment_v3.docx (draft amendment), throughput_modeling_20270602.pdf (pdf)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-02T10:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: BlueCrest renewal — pricing/negotiation notes

Markus / Aditya — quick internal notes before we send final.

- Pricing: €2.95/hr/GPU for the incremental 16 sounds OK as an anchor. If procurement pushes back, we can offer a time-limited uplift discount (2.7€/hr) if they sign a firm 18-month term. Keep the 3% longer-term concession as a bargaining chip.
- SLA language: make the throughput guarantee explicit with measurement windows and remedy (credit) tiers rather than penalties. Example: if monthly verified throughput falls below 95% of target, BlueCrest gets a credit equal to X% of incremental reserved spend for that month. Aditya — can you define X based on modeling?
- Migration credit: 50% credit for the first 30 days is generous; suggest we cap the credit to the equivalent cost of ~8 GPUs during the window to limit exposure.
- Ops dependencies: Ask BlueCrest to confirm model mix (seq lengths and batch modes). If their traffic is skewed to long-range seqs, throughput numbers change materially.

I'll prepare a short commercial redline doc and loop legal after you confirm.

Laura Bennett
Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference

(On a side note: avoid offering hourly credits that scale linearly with peak — cap it.)

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <elena.park@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-05T16:45:00Z
Subject: Renewal amendment and next steps (16→32 GPUs)

Hi Elena — attaching the updated amendment and a short throughput summary from Aditya. Summary of changes since my earlier note:

- Commercial: incremental 16 GPUs at €2.95/hr/GPU. Option: sign an 18-month term and receive €0.10/hr/GPU additional discount (net €2.85/hr).
- Ramp: migration window credit structured as a 50% credit for month 1, capped to the equivalent cost of 8 GPUs during that window.
- Throughput SLA: target = 2.1x current verified peak; verification via weekly measurement windows and monthly aggregation. Remedy = billing credit tiers (5% credit if 90–95% attainment, 12% credit if 80–90%, escalated review if <80%).
- Acceptance path: we propose a commercial call Thursday 10:00am BST and 7 business-day turnaround for procurement to provide redlines.

I’ve attached: redwood_amendment_v3.docx (amendment with highlighted redlines) and throughput_modeling_20270602.pdf (token mix assumptions and verification methodology).

Please let me know if that aligns with procurement’s expectations or if you want us to present to them directly.

Thanks — look forward to closing this quickly so your infra team can begin the migration plan.

Best,
Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Markus.Klein@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_amendment_v3.docx (draft amendment), throughput_modeling_20270602.pdf (pdf)]
